# Thought Process: DFS Algorithm

#### Course: DSA with C++

## Thought Process: DFS Algorithm

To implement the DFS algorithm, we need the following:

- An empty vector to keep track of the traversal sequence.
- An unordered set to keep track of visited vertices.
- A stack to track the vertices to visit and push the starting vertex into it.

```cpp
vector<int> traversal_seq;
unordered_set<int> visited;
stack<int> to_visit;
to_visit.push(start_vertex);
```

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

Now that we have our variables ready, we'll implement the DFS algorithm in the following way.

1. Assign the top vertex as the current vertex and then remove it from the stack.

```cpp
int current_vertex = to_visit.top();
to_visit.pop();
```

2. Traverse the current vertex if it hasn't been traversed and add its neighbors to the stack.

This steps requires you to do the following:

- Add current_vertex to traversal_seq.
- Add current_vertex to the visited set.
- Push the neighbors of current_vertex to the stack if they have not been visited.

```cpp
if (!visited.count(current_vertex)) {
    traversal_seq.push_back(current_vertex);
    visited.insert(current_vertex);

    for (auto neighbor : adj_list[current_vertex]) {
        if (!visited.count(neighbor)) {
            to_visit.push(neighbor);
        }
    }
}
```

3. Repeat steps 1 and 2 as long as the stack is not empty.

```cpp
while (!to_visit.empty()) {
    // Code of steps 1 and 2       
}
```

Now, we'll wrap all the code we've written inside the dfs_traversal() method, which will take start_vertex as an argument.

```cpp
vector<int> dfs_traversal(int start_vertex) {
    // Code from above steps
}
```
